owner_decisions: 1. Court unit for the six. Verified arithmetic: the court (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:327-336,382-401) keys on shared ENTRY days, closed legs only, symmetric-trims n-2 and needs t >= 1.8 plus own-mean >= +3/day plus both halves positive; only names ending _W get the weekly unit (:369-379). At <= 3 picks/week per name that is 3-8 weeks to 8 shared days per picker, and t >= 1.8 on 6 trimmed diffs with a ~60-pt per-trade sigma needs roughly +44/day — the cited +12%/trade edge has about 1-in-7 power, while six correlated siblings partitioning one candidate list give a 7-33% chance of crowning noise. Options: (a) one STUDENT family book for the court (weekly unit, family k=18/week, placebo bar from the placebo_t95 machinery at :83-94), per-model split published as diagnostics — RECOMMENDED; (b) six individual day-unit books as ordered, accepting the court is a catastrophe detector, not a skill detector, at this cadence; (c) give each picker the _W weekly unit.

2. Six configurations vs the pre-registered protocol. scripts/student_formula_sim.py:10-11 pre-registered that the holdout is touched ONCE by the single winner; six of 72 configs are going live, so five carry only selection-biased search-window numbers and the family has a multiple-testing history the court is not told about. Options: (a) audition all six as ordered, with 'holdout: not touched' and search-window rank stated per picker in the roster note; (b) audition the pre-registered winner plus the one least-correlated sibling (best PWIN/BASE and best EXPRET/WIDE), keep the other four as shadow books (scored and logged via condition A, no orders) — RECOMMENDED; (c) audition the winner only.

3. Monday path if the honest re-export (required item 6) is not finished by Sunday night. 4. Automatic pull rule. Should a picker whose walk-forward AUC on the honest columns (printed by the re-export) is <= 0.50, or whose EXPRET OOS mean is <= 0, be pulled from the block before it trades? RECOMMENDED: yes, automatically, with the number in the roster note; the alternative is to audition it anyway as a control for the court.

5. Roster size vs ROADMAP #33. The owner fixed the roster at SEVEN on 2026-09-10 for throughput. The one-seat design in required item 4 makes it eight and costs one probe's attempts; six separate seats make it thirteen and cost the fixed five roughly half their cycles. Confirm the one-seat design is acceptable as the implementation of 'six pickers'; if six separate seats are insisted on, accept the throughput regression explicitly and have it printed in the '0 entries' line every starved cycle.

findings.title: Weekly-budget gate references an unbound name `log`: the first STUDENT_ probe reached raises NameError and aborts the rest of the roster loop every cycle
findings.attack: Enable the spec block (currently absent, so the wiring is inert) and the first STUDENT_ entry reached in `_order` evaluates `_student_week_used(_pname, log)` at line 2637. `log` is never bound in run_scheduled_cycle (symtable: resolved as a global, module-level absent; the book is loaded as `_plog` at 2484 and `log_r` at 2269). NameError is raised at the call site, before the function's own try/except, before any attempt is spent. It exits the `for` at 2632 through the `finally` at 2752 into `except Exception as _pe` at 2754, which prints one generic 'probe skipped (fail-open): NameError'. Every probe after that student in the rotation gets zero attempts. Students sit at `_rest[0:6]`, so on 6 of 11 start indices the fixed five (BULL_DIP, DIP_CONVEXITY, DIP_CONF_MILD, WINNER_PROFILE, FOLLOW_CALLS) receive nothing after the control; on the other 5 the tail is cut. Net effect: zero student fills ever, plus a rotation-dependent blackout of the roster the owner just trimmed for throughput, reported as a benign fail-open. Nothing catches it: MOT 1147-1149 asserts the literal string '_student_week_used(_pname, log)' (enshrining the bug), MOT 1153-1154 skips every model-file check because `_stu.get('enabled')` is false on a spec with no student block (so the suite is green with no block and no model files present), and regime_drill 164-197 calls `_student_filter` directly and never executes the loop.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2635-2638 (call with `log`); :2484 (`_plog` is the loaded book); :2269 (`log_r`); :2632 (for), :2752 (finally), :2754-2755 (outer except, generic print); :2507-2510 (students at _rest[0:6]); :2608 (`_rot`); v11_mot_harness.py:1147-1149 (string-presence check), :1153-1154 (model checks gated on enabled); scripts/regime_drill.py:164-197 (filter called directly, loop never run); reports/fade_meta/ has no student_*.json; fade_book_spec.json has no probe.student block
findings.fix: Bind `log = _plog` (or pass `_plog`) at 2637. Add a drill that runs run_scheduled_cycle's probe loop with a fake enabled student block and asserts a probe AFTER the student still receives attempts. Change MOT 1153-1165 to FAIL, not skip, when the branch claims the students are live and the block or the six model files are absent.

findings.title: Bear stand-down runs after the sensor sweep and is fail-open on a None regime - the only regime-conditioned probe that trades through a regime-feed outage
findings.attack: The stand-down lives inside `_pf` (497-501), which enter_proactive_set calls at 1382 only after `collect_metadata` at 1376. The fixed probes' candidate-independent regime gate was hoisted to 2640-2647 precisely because the panel (2026-09-01) caught this pattern burning the whole attempt budget on wrong-regime days. On a BEAR day each student reached burns up to `_PROBE_MAX_ATT`=4 sweeps to learn a free fact; six students can consume the full 10-attempt budget while BULL_DIP/DIP_CONF_MILD stand down for free. Worse: spy_regime is fail-OPEN by design (fade_book.py:20, returns None on any Alpaca bars error), and `None == 'BEAR'` is False, so on an outage the charter guard silently vanishes while `spy_dist50()` returns None and the `reg` feature (line 488) becomes NaN routed down the majority branch. BULL_DIP, DIP_CONVEXITY and DIP_CONF_MILD all stand down on None (`!= _rg_need`); the student is the one regime-conditioned probe that keeps trading, on a blinded regime feature, with its guard off.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:497-501 (stand-down inside _pf), :1376 (sweep), :1382 (filter after sweep), :2640-2647 (hoisted gate + panel comment), :522 (_PROBE_MAX_ATT=4), :488 (reg from spy_dist50); fade_book.py:17-21 and :48-51 (fail-OPEN None, cached per day), :53-56 (spy_dist50 returns cached dist, None when unknown)
findings.fix: Hoist `if bear_standdown and fade_book.spy_regime() in (None, 'BEAR'): continue` beside the weekly-budget check at 2635, before any sweep; keep `_pf` purely model-based. Add the None-regime case to regime_drill scenario 6 and assert the probe stands down.

findings.title: Six pickers, one candidate pool, one identical feature vector, six separate sweeps - the throughput fix of 2026-09-10 is undone by construction
findings.attack: All six STUDENT_ probes draw from the same `_PRICEY_CANDS[:14]` (2652-2653) and `_student_score` uses `name` only to select the model (477-493): md and vector are identical across the six for a given ticker. `collect_metadata` (302-317) has no per-ticker cache and is paid per attempt at 1376; skip propagation (2721-2724) covers spread/metadata/premium codes only, so 'scored below threshold' is never shared. On the 6 of 11 start indices that land in the student block: the control takes 1-4 attempts, student A sweeps pool[0:4], student B re-sweeps the same pool[0:4] with different trees, student C gets the leftovers - two or three sweeps per ticker for information one sweep already contained, and zero attempts for the fixed five on those cycles. With loose thresholds (see the calibration finding) the students also take both `_cyc` entry slots. The owner cut the roster to seven on 2026-09-10 so each survivor fills 2-3x faster; the design doc (section 2) specified ONE probe with ordinary attempt accounting; the build adds six contiguous seats the next day, ahead of the fixed five in rotation order.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2507-2510 (six seats at _rest[0:6]), :2652-2653 (shared pool), :477-493 (score depends on name only via the model), :302-317 (no md cache), :1376 (sweep per attempt), :522 (4 per probe), :2633 (10 per cycle, 2 entries), :2608 (_rot over len(_rest)=11), :2721-2724 (propagation codes); reports/student_wiring_design_2026-09-11.md:23-30 (one probe, standard attempt accounting)
findings.fix: One sweep per ticker scores all six models: pre-score the pool once per cycle (one collect_metadata, six predicts, cached md per ticker) and enter for the best-passing student; or collapse the six into ONE roster seat 'STUDENT' whose filter takes argmax over the six models with per-model weekly budgets, so the block costs one probe's attempts. Print the per-probe attempt split in the 'probes: 0 entries' line at 2743 so the starvation is visible.

findings.title: Live vector blacks out 5 of 22 features the model was trained on; k-thresholds are in-sample quantiles on full vectors; the spec threshold override is unit-blind; the parity MOT is structurally unable to see any of it
findings.attack: `_student_score` passes `None` for quote_bid (484) so spread_frac is NaN (student_features.py:97-98); it passes `None, None` for delta/gamma (488-489) so delta_prev, gamma_prev, abs_delta_prev are NaN (student_features.py:79-80); price_drift is NaN by construction (student_features.py:102). The archive builder populates all five (student_asof_build.py:40-47; student_features.py:57-59). For a feature with no NaN at fit time sklearn stores missing_go_to_left = 'larger child', which is exactly the `ml` bit the exporter carries (student_features.py:115-116), so every live NaN rides the majority branch of every split on those features - deterministic, but not the distribution the thresholds were computed on. The thresholds are quantiles of the model's own IN-SAMPLE scores on the trailing 60 sessions of the training set (student_export.py:68-78). So the 'k picks/week' calibration does not bound the live pass rate in either direction; the only brakes are k_per_week=3, per-day 5 and 2 per cycle, i.e. up to $18k/week of paper fills that the court will judge as evidence for a picker that never saw its own features. The spec override `cfg.get('threshold')` (505-506) is applied regardless of `kind`: an EXPRET regressor's score is a raw return clipped to [-100,300] (student_export.py:60-62,72), so a `threshold: 0.60` copied from ROADMAP.md:279's 'scored 0.60+' admits any candidate with expected return above 0.6%. The MOT parity fixture (v11_mot_harness.py:1133-1136) calls the live builder with bid=5.0 and delta/gamma None on BOTH sides and drops every NaN pair from the comparison - it tests a call signature the engine never makes and is blind to features NaN on one side only. `parity_max_err` is computed at export (student_export.py:79-83) but never asserted there; the only check (v11_mot_harness.py:1163-1165) is skipped while the spec block is absent.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:484, :488-489, :505-506; src/student_features.py:79-80, :97-98, :102, :115-116; scripts/student_asof_build.py:40-47; scripts/student_export.py:60-62, :68-78, :79-83; v11_mot_harness.py:1133-1136, :1153-1154, :1163-1165; ROADMAP.md:279
findings.fix: Feed the live bid: `_live_spread_pct` (527-541) already fetches bp/ap for the alert contract - cache the pair, not just spread%. Either fetch delta/gamma from the Alpaca option snapshot for the trigger contract or drop spread_frac/price_drift/delta_prev/gamma_prev/abs_delta_prev from FEATS and retrain so training and live are the same vector. Assert parity_max_err <= 1e-4 in the exporter (refuse to write the file otherwise). Make `_pf` reject a spec threshold whose unit does not match `kind` (classifier requires 0<thr<1; regressor requires a return-point threshold). Rewrite the MOT parity fixture to call asof_from_alert with the exact argument shape the engine uses and to FAIL on any feature NaN on one side only.

findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2479 (outer try), :2509 (.keys()), :2637 (int parse), :510 (float(thr)), :2707-2708 (attempt charged), :2713-2714 (silent continue), :509 (p written before compare), :2732-2734 (stamp); reports/student_wiring_design_2026-09-11.md:30, :58-59

findings.title: The six pickers exist only in prose: no spec block, no model files, no corpus, and the court would never judge them anyway
findings.attack: In this checkout fade_book_spec.json has no probe.student block at all (python dump: probe.student -> None), so the roster comprehension at sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2509-2510 adds zero STUDENT_ entries, student_export.py:45-47 prints 'no student probes in the spec' and exports nothing, and reports/fade_meta/ holds no student_*.json. The MOT's model-file, 22-feature, thresholds and 1e-4 parity checks sit inside `if _stu.get('enabled')` (v11_mot_harness.py:1153-1165), so a green MOT proves nothing about six pickers - it proves the block is absent. Worse, even once the block is hand-added: the promotion court iterates ONLY probe.priority (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:316-317, 358) and nothing in the wiring adds STUDENT_ names to priority (spec priority = CREDIT_SPREAD_W ... BULL_DIP_X), so 'same court as every probe' is false - the pickers would trade $1,000 auditions indefinitely with no verdict clock. And the nightly gate page greps the lab file for the literal '"STUDENT_SELECT"' (scripts/fade_meta.py:200) which this wiring never defines, so 'STUDENT GATE MET ... wiring session is owed' will keep paging the owner weekly after the pickers are live. A hostile room cannot audit six names, targets, cohorts, exits, k values or thresholds that are not in the repo; nor can the as-of search be reproduced (student_asof_build.py:18 reads a file that does not exist here).
findings.fix: One commit, before any live cycle: (1) the probe.student block with all six entries (model path, target, cohort, exit_label, k_per_week) plus the six exported JSON files plus the search report and the sha256 of student_asof_v3.jsonl the models were trained on; (2) either append the six names to probe.priority or make the court iterate probe.student.probes as well; (3) flip the MOT so that when sandbox_proactive_lab.py contains `def _student_score` and probe.student is absent/disabled the check FAILS rather than skips; (4) retarget the fade_meta gate page to `probe.student.enabled`. Until that commit lands, the honest statement is 'zero pickers are live'.
findings.evidence: fade_book_spec.json (probe.student absent); sandbox_proactive_lab.py:445-451, 2509-2510; scripts/student_export.py:45-47; v11_mot_harness.py:1153-1165; scripts/sunday_boundary.py:316-317, 358, 382-384; scripts/fade_meta.py:200-206; scripts/student_asof_build.py:18-19

findings.title: The live vector is not the training vector: 5 of 22 features are permanently NaN live and the 'as-of' block is a different quantity under the same name; the parity fixture is built so it cannot notice
findings.attack: _student_score passes quote_bid=None (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:486) so spread_frac is NaN on every live row even though the alert row carried bid (lab:1965 computes _qb for the 2% check but the aggx 'alert' dict at 1983-1991 never stores it); it passes delta_prev=None, gamma_prev=None (lab:489) so delta_prev, gamma_prev, abs_delta_prev are NaN on every live row; price_drift is NaN by design (src/student_features.py:102). Training populated all five from contracts_daily and the print NBBO (scripts/student_asof_build.py:40-46, 57-58; student_features.py:57-59). HistGradientBoosting routes NaN by missing_go_to_left learned where missing was rare (features.py:134-135), so every live row takes branches the training distribution almost never took - the live score distribution is shifted and the k-per-week thresholds (calibrated on full-feature scores) no longer mean k/week. Separately, the shared names hide different quantities: archive cum_prem/n_prints/cum_size/ask_share are the per-print stream up to the 50k crossing (features.py:40-62, so cum_prem is by construction ~50k-ish), archive mins_since_first is minutes from the day's FIRST print; live cum_prem/n_prints are the UW alert cluster's total_premium/trade_count (50-400k by the pool filter, lab:1974-1988) and first_seen is the earliest created_at within the CURRENT API page only (lab:1989-1991), typically minutes not hours. The spec's own dip_conf_mild note already concedes per-alert vs daily is 'an approximation'. The MOT parity fixture (v11_mot_harness.py:1124-1135) hardcodes total_premium=57000 equal to the archive cum, passes quote_bid=5.0 (which the engine never does), and skips every pair where either side is NaN - it is a tautology, and the drill scenario (scripts/regime_drill.py:165-190) uses the same synthetic alert with an empty tree list. No live-path test has ever produced a real 22-float vector from a real alert.
findings.fix: (1) Store the alert's bid in the aggx alert dict and pass it; source delta/gamma from the sweep (or drop those three features from FEATS and retrain - a feature the live path can never supply is dead weight and a silent distribution shift). (2) Replace the fixture with a real parity test: replay one archived contract-day's flow_prints as a synthetic alert stream through asof_from_alert and assert the SAME numbers as asof_from_prints, or admit in the model card that the two builders measure different things and retrain on alert-shaped features. (3) Passively log the full live vector and score for EVERY scored candidate (harvest-style, never on the trade path) so the week-1 live feature distribution can be compared against the training marginals before any fill is treated as evidence.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:484-490, 1965, 1974-1991; src/student_features.py:40-62, 83-103, 127-139; scripts/student_asof_build.py:40-46, 57-58; v11_mot_harness.py:1124-1135; scripts/regime_drill.py:165-190; fade_book_spec.json dip_conf_mild.evidence 'HONESTY NOTE'

findings.title: Training cohort is selected on end-of-day information and on both sides; the live pool is calls-only, per-alert, top-14 by premium, and gated on the fade book being LIVE
findings.attack: The as-of build only swaps the feature vector; it inherits the v3 row SET (scripts/student_asof_build.py:22-24), and that set is chosen from contracts_daily by END-OF-DAY totals: total_premium between 50k and 1M and ask_volume > bid_volume at the close, EOD NBBO spread <= 2%, one row per OCC ever (scripts/probe_tuner.py:152-158, 163-165, 180). A contract-day is in the training population only if it ENDED ask-dominant and in-band - that is not knowable at the qualifying print, so 'every feature is knowable at the alert moment' is true of the columns and false of the rows: P(win) is calibrated on a survivor population. The live pool is _PRICEY_CANDS: calls only (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1961, flow_type hardcoded 'call' at 1977), per-alert premium 50-400k, ask-side > bid-side at alert time, spread <= 2% at alert time, DTE >= 7, one alert per ticker (max premium), top 14 by premium (lab:2044), read by every STUDENT_ probe (lab:2652-2653). The AFFORD cohort the models were fitted on (student_export.py:31-32) is both sides and any premium, so the side feature is a constant +1 live and the model's put-side structure never fires; the holdout '+12%/trade' was earned on both-sides picks from the survivor population. _PRICEY_CANDS is assigned only inside `if fade_book.active()` (lab:2036-2044) despite the _student_cfg comment claiming the roster runs regardless of the fade book (lab:447-449): status OFF -> silent empty pool, no loud line. bear_standdown (lab:500-501) then removes the one regime whose positivity was the search's selection flag (student_formula_sim.py:21-24, 225), so the live verdict can only ever be a BULL/MILD verdict on an 'all-regimes' pick.
findings.fix: Rebuild the training rows with the live gate applied at alert time (calls, alert-cluster premium 50-400k, ask>bid at that moment, spread <= 2% at that moment, first qualifying alert per ticker-day, no EOD filters), re-run the search on that cohort, and only then export. Populate _PRICEY_CANDS outside the fade_book.active() branch or print a loud 'student pool empty: fade book OFF' line. State in the roster note that the picker is being judged on a calls-only bull/mild slice of what was scored.

findings.title: Court arithmetic: 8 shared single-trade days at <=3 picks/week is 4-8 weeks to a verdict, a trimmed t>=1.8 on 6 observations is powered for a +40-50/day edge not +12, six correlated siblings share one pool and censor each other, and the live picker is not the simulated picker
findings.attack: The court keys returns by ENTRY day, closed legs only, shared with EXEC_BASELINE, symmetric-trims to n-2, and requires t >= 1.8 plus own-mean >= +3/day plus both halves positive (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:327-336, 382-401). Students get the DAY unit - only names ending _W get the weekly unit the court itself introduced because 'day-shared accrual starved them ... months to the bar' (sunday_boundary.py:369-379). With k_per_week 3 (lab:2637) the bar is 3 weeks best case and realistically 4-8: rotation over ~12 roster slots at 2 entries per cycle (lab:2605-2607, 2633), all six pickers reading the same 14 names in premium order (lab:2653), and the first sibling to fill an underlying blocking the other five for up to 5 days via _open_tk (lab:2664-2665) and the one-record-per-contract guard (lab:1484-1505). Each shared day is then ONE leg's return vs the control's day-mean; with a per-trade sigma of ~50-70 pts on -50/+50 exits, t >= 1.8 on 6 trimmed diffs needs a mean edge of roughly 1.8 x 60 / sqrt(6) ~ +44 pts/day. The evidence that justified going live is +12%/trade, weekly t 1.45 (below the court's own bar): power ~1 in 7. Under the null P(t>=1.8 | df 5) ~ 7% per picker, so six pickers give a 7-33% chance of promoting a lucky sibling while the true +12 edge fails 6 times in 7 - the court is more likely to crown noise than skill, and the trim deletes the jackpot day that would otherwise carry a picker across. The pickers are not six independent samples: their books are a rotation-ordered partition of one candidate list, so A's verdict is conditional on B-F's fills. And the sim's pick rule was 'best-scored first within a day, threshold on prior OOS scores' (student_formula_sim.py:178-207); live is 'first candidate in premium order that clears the threshold, whenever rotation reaches this picker' (lab:2653, 2661-2712) - the audition is of a different selection rule than the one whose holdout was cited. What month one can prove: catastrophic failure (own-mean far below the floor) or a jackpot. What it cannot prove: a +12/trade edge, or which of the six carries it.
findings.fix: Judge the six as ONE family: either pool them into a single STUDENT_FAMILY book for the court (one verdict, 6x the fill rate, k=18/week family budget), or give each picker the _W weekly unit with a placebo-army bar computed for 6 books on the same days (the placebo_t95 machinery at sunday_boundary.py:83-94 exists for the fade book; use it here). Pre-register the minimum detectable edge and print 'weeks to verdict at current fill rate' in the Sunday boundary. If six must audition, cap to the two least-correlated (best PWIN/BASE and best EXPRET/WIDE) and freeze the rest as shadow books. Implement within-day best-score-first (score the whole pool, sort by score, enter the top) so the live rule matches the simulated one.

findings.title: Thresholds are calibrated on in-sample tail scores (the search never did that), the freeze is a 120-day stand-down not a pin, a re-export silently changes the model under the court, and the live model is not the model the holdout scored
findings.attack: student_export.py:68-78 sets each k threshold as a quantile of the FINAL model's scores on the trailing 60 sessions of its OWN training rows and claims 'as the search did for its first window'; the search's pick_weekly used -inf until 100 prior OOS scores existed, then the 0.9 quantile of PRIOR out-of-sample scores, never in-sample (student_formula_sim.py:190-198). In-sample boosted scores are more separated, so the live bar is stricter than the simulated bar and the realised fill rate is unknown - and with the 5 always-NaN features shrinking live scores toward the baseline (finding 2) it is unknowable without logging rejected-candidate scores, which the wiring does not do (only fills get student_p, lab:2732-2734), so the 'calibration audit' promised in the design cannot be run. Teacher-freeze: the export overwrites reports/fade_meta/student_<NAME>.json in place (export:87), not the dated file + pinned filename the design section 5 required; the only freeze mechanism is max_model_age_days 120 (lab:465-466), which stands the probe DOWN at day 121 regardless of court state, mid-case. The export docstring says re-export 'on the quarterly cadence'; the design says 'only on a completed verdict'; neither rule is in code. When a re-export does happen, the court's evidence clock reads only probe.tuning.<name>.applied (sunday_boundary.py:356-366) - the export writes no such stamp, so days earned by the old model pool with the new one; the student_model date on records (lab:2734) is never read by the court. Finally train_end defaults to 'all' (export:49-51, 86): the live model is fitted through the holdout, so '+12%/trade t 1.45' describes a model that is not trading, on a population that is not the live pool (finding 3), under a selection rule that is not the live rule (finding 4). The pre-registration allowed ONE winner to touch the holdout (formula_sim:10-11, 305-306); six configurations from 72 are going live, so five of them carry only selection-biased search-window numbers and the family has a multiple-testing history the court is not told about.
findings.fix: Calibrate thresholds on the walk-forward OOS stream's last 60 sessions (the streams already exist in student_formula_sim.fit_stream), never on in-sample scores. Write dated model files and pin the filename in the spec; have the export write probe.tuning.<name>.applied = trained date so the court's clock restarts on any model change, and have the court also split on the record's student_model stamp. Replace the 120-day stand-down with 'no re-export until the court returns a verdict' in code (export refuses while a case is open unless STUDENT_FORCE_REFIT=1 by owner order). Publish per picker: which of the 72 it was, its search-window rank, and 'holdout: not touched' for the five non-winners. Log every scored candidate's vector and score passively so calibration can be audited on non-picks.

findings.title: Five of the 22 features are structurally NaN on the live path (spread_frac, price_drift, delta_prev, gamma_prev, abs_delta_prev) - the live vector is out of the training support and the pick set collapses
findings.attack: The engine passes quote_bid=None (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:486), so asof_from_alert's spread_frac is always NaN (src/student_features.py:97-98); price_drift is hard-coded NaN (src/student_features.py:102); delta/gamma are passed as None, None (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:490), so delta_prev, gamma_prev and abs_delta_prev are NaN on every live row. In the AFFORD training cohort (17,987 rows on the VPS as-of corpus) spread_frac and price_drift are 0.0% NaN and the greeks are 29.6% NaN - and the greeks are co-missing with OI/IV (0 rows have OI present and delta missing, because all four come from the same contracts_daily row: scripts/student_asof_build.py:40-46,57). Live, 100% of rows have OI/IV present and greeks missing: a combination the trees never saw. A model fitted exactly as scripts/student_export.py:65 does puts 210 of its 1,087 splits on these five features (delta 67, spread_frac 56, price_drift 36, gamma 29, abs_delta 22); the delta missing-routes (25 left / 42 right) were learned on the 'no prior-day row' subgroup, which is the worse subgroup (BASE mean -8.08 vs -4.57). spread_frac is doubly loaded: it is the exact exit haircut applied to every training label (scripts/probe_tuner.py:183,187), so its 56 splits partly encode label mechanics the live path can never see. Walk-forward test (train < 2026-06-01, 1,150 OOS rows): the export-style k3 threshold picks 17 rows with true features and 1 row with live-shaped features (overlap 1); mean P shifts 0.458 to 0.443. The k-per-week thresholds (scripts/student_export.py:70-78) are calibrated on true-feature scores, so live pick rates and the weekly budget are mis-set as well. Caveat for the room: in that same window the picker's OOS AUC is 0.460 even with true features, so parity is necessary, not sufficient.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:486,490; src/student_features.py:97-98,102; scripts/student_asof_build.py:40-46,57; scripts/student_export.py:65,70-78; scripts/probe_tuner.py:183,187; VPS as-of corpus stats: greeks NaN 29.6%, spread_frac/price_drift NaN 0.0%, OI-present-and-delta-missing = 0 rows; split counts 67/56/36/29/22 of 1,087; walk-forward picks 17 vs 1
findings.fix: Store the alert's bid alongside alert_ask in the aggx block (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1963,1981-1983) and pass it at :486. Compute delta/gamma at scoring time from strike, underlying_price, iv_start and dte (Black-Scholes, no dependency) or pull the contract's greeks from UW, and stamp them on the record. Either drop price_drift from FEATS and retrain, or derive it from the earliest alert's price for that option_chain in the pull. Export a per-feature training NaN-rate manifest with the model and make _student_score fail CLOSED (loud line, no trade) when any feature with training NaN-rate < 1% is NaN live. Recalibrate thresholds on live-shaped vectors, not archive vectors.

findings.title: reg / sp / smd in training are computed from the ENTRY-DAY CLOSE - post-entry information in the three most-split features, measured differently live
findings.attack: probe_tuner.py's smad() sets o[x] from c[x], the close of day x, over a window that includes x (scripts/probe_tuner.py:63-66), and the corpus keys smd/reg/sp on the entry day (scripts/probe_tuner.py:162). Entry is the ask at the qualifying print + 10 min (scripts/probe_tuner.py:128,180) and the label window starts there (scripts/probe_tuner.py:187), so the same-day close move sits inside every return the model is trained against. Measured on the as-of corpus: for calls, the top tercile of delta-smd (D minus the ticker's prior corpus day) has BASE mean +5.68 / 55.3% wins vs -4.24 / 46.6% in the bottom tercile; for puts the sign flips (-18.00 vs -9.10), exactly as a leak and not momentum predicts; reg and sp show the same side-flipping correlation (calls +0.05/+0.06, puts -0.10/-0.11). reg, sp and smd are the #1, #2 and #5 most-split features (116 + 95 + 77 = 27% of all splits). The live builder feeds intraday running values instead: fade_book.spy_dist50 uses bars with no end bound and cl[-1] (fade_book.py:31,37,44), macro_technical uses spot = closes[-1] from an unbounded pull (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:134,146), and _sma_distance likewise (sandbox_v11_sensors.py:39-62); harvest records show macro.spot within 0.25% of the live underlying on half the rows, i.e. not a prior close. So the live values are a different quantity from the trained ones, and whatever part of the backtest edge came from the leak cannot transfer. The affordable-band formula-search winners were selected on the same leaky columns, so this taints the model choice, not only its fit. This contradicts design section 7 ('No label leak').
findings.evidence: scripts/probe_tuner.py:63-66,128,162,180,187; fade_book.py:31,37,44,53; sandbox_proactive_lab.py:134,146,488-489; sandbox_v11_sensors.py:39-62; reports/student_wiring_design_2026-09-11.md section 7; VPS corpus: calls top/bottom tercile delta-smd +5.68/-4.24, puts -18.00/-9.10; split counts reg 116, sp 95, smd 77
findings.fix: Rebuild the corpus with reg/sp/smd defined at D-1 close (shift smad by one day) or at the qualifying-print intraday price from hourly_paths.db, re-run the formula search and OOF scores on the honest columns, then re-export. Make the live builder use the identical definition: bound the bar pulls at yesterday (or drop the last bar when its date is today) so both sides are the D-1 close and knowable at the alert; add a MOT check that no regime input carries today's date.

findings.title: Training population is selected on end-of-day facts (day premium band, day ask_volume > bid_volume, EOD spread) - the as-of build inherits an EOD-conditioned cohort despite claiming EOD totals never enter
findings.attack: student_asof_build.py reads probe_tuner_rows_v3 (scripts/student_asof_build.py:18,23), whose rows were admitted only when the contract-day's total_premium was in [50k, 1M] and its day ask_volume > bid_volume with an EOD NBBO spread <= 2% (scripts/probe_tuner.py:155-156, spread check below it). None of that is knowable at the alert moment. Measured on 6,000 corpus rows joined back to contracts_daily: the median EOD-total / as-of cum_prem ratio is 3.24x, 70.9% of rows at least doubled after the as-of moment, 100% ended ask-heavy by construction, and 788 rows (13%) were bid-heavy at the as-of moment (ask_share < 0.5) yet remain in the corpus only because the day finished ask-heavy. The live cohort cannot condition on continued ask-side flow, so its base rate is worse than the training base rate and the P thresholds (calibrated on the conditioned cohort) are optimistic. The design's parity promise (section 3) and the build docstring (scripts/student_asof_build.py:1-4) are both contradicted.
findings.evidence: scripts/student_asof_build.py:1-4,18,23; scripts/probe_tuner.py:155-156,162; sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1972 (live requires only the alert's ask-side > bid-side); VPS join: EOD/as-of ratio q50 3.24x, 70.9% >= 2x, 788/6000 as-of bid-heavy rows kept by the EOD gate
findings.fix: Re-select the corpus at the as-of moment only: as-of cum_prem >= 50k, as-of ask_share > 0.5 (mirrors the live _asp > _bsp gate), print-level spread <= 2% at the qualifying print; drop every EOD gate. Retrain, re-threshold and publish the base-rate shift so the court's expectations are set on the live-shaped population.

findings.title: Flow-block features are different objects on the two sides: day-cumulative-at-50k-crossing (archive) vs one UW alert burst (live); iv_prev prior-close vs intraday; oi lag unverified
findings.attack: cum_prem archive = cumulative premium at the first crossing of 50k (src/student_features.py:32-60; median 75k, q95 237k); live = the alert's own total_premium after max-per-ticker selection in 50-400k (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1976,1983). n_prints archive = prints to the crossing, q05-q95 = {1,2} with all 15 splits routing missing-left; live = UW trade_count per alert (5-7 in cached samples), so every live value beyond 2 falls off the training support. cum_size archive (median 116) vs alert total_size is a different object of similar magnitude, and vol_oi_asof / prem_oi_asof inherit both mismatches. ask_share archive = share of premium in prints where ask_vol >= bid_vol, ties counted as ask (scripts/uw_flow_prints.py:103; src/student_features.py:47) vs live ask/(ask+bid) excluding mid premium (src/student_features.py:100) - only 5 splits, low impact. iv_prev archive = D-1 EOD implied_volatility (scripts/student_asof_build.py:40) vs live iv_start = the alert's intraday IV (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:490); 93 splits (#3 feature), and intraday IV on a sweep day sits above the prior close, so live rows shift on every IV split. oi_prev archive = the D-1 row's open_interest vs live = the alert's open_interest (the day's published OI); design section 3 asserts 'same quantity' without evidence - a one-day lag either way is unresolved. hour (both UTC), dow, dte, side, mins_since_first (median 0 on both sides) and entry_ask (EWMA-NBBO vs instantaneous ask, scripts/uw_flow_prints.py:101-102) are acceptable.
findings.evidence: src/student_features.py:32-60,47,83-102; sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1976,1983-1991,490; scripts/uw_flow_prints.py:101-103; scripts/student_asof_build.py:40; reports/student_wiring_design_2026-09-11.md section 3; VPS corpus quantiles cum_prem 52k/61k/75k/97k/237k, n_prints 1/1/2/2/2, ask_share q25 0.87
findings.fix: Define each flow feature once in terms the live path can reproduce (alert-level: the alert's total_premium, trade_count, total_size, ask/(ask+bid)) and build the ARCHIVE side by replaying UW's alert aggregation window on the prints instead of day-cumulative sums; pin iv_prev to one timing on both sides (D-1 EOD via the UW contract endpoint live, or intraday on both); settle OI semantics with one UW query per side and document it; retrain after the redefinition and re-run the walk-forward pick comparison.

findings.title: The MOT parity fixture is vacuous: it hand-builds an alert equal to the print block, passes a bid the engine never passes, and skips every NaN pair - so none of the above can fail it; no model files or spec block exist yet for the model checks to run
findings.attack: v11_mot_harness.py:1128 constructs the alert with total_premium 57000, total_size 110, trade_count 2 - literally the values asof_from_prints produced - and :1130 passes quote_bid=5.0, whereas the engine passes None (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:486); both sides pass delta/gamma None; and the comparison at :1135 drops price_drift and any pair where either value is NaN (a == a and b == b), so a live vector with five NaNs and redefined cum_prem passes 'parity'. The fixture proves vector() is deterministic, not that the engine's inputs match the archive's. The model-file checks are gated on _stu.get('enabled') (v11_mot_harness.py:1154); on the VPS checkout there is no reports/fade_meta/student_*.json and fade_book_spec.json has no probe.student block, so those checks currently never execute and the wiring is ahead of the export.
findings.evidence: v11_mot_harness.py:1128,1130,1135,1154; sandbox_proactive_lab.py:486; VPS: reports/fade_meta/student_*.json absent, spec probe.student = null
findings.fix: Drive the fixture through _student_score itself on a frozen md + candidate (the engine's real call path) and compare against asof_from_prints + vector for the same contract-day; treat NaN-vs-value as a mismatch; assert no feature with training NaN-rate < 1% is NaN in the live vector; assert live cum_prem/n_prints/cum_size fall inside the training q01-q99 support. Make the model-file and threshold checks unconditional once the spec block lands, and add a regime-drill scenario with the live-shaped (NaN-bearing) vector.
